machine: 8-core/16-thread desktop CPU, NVMe SSDs, mid-range discrete GPU, Windows 11
noise: Runs were taken on a busy machine, so treat results as upper bounds with ±20–30% run-to-run noise. Ranges are the spread across runs.
methodology: Release builds only. Criterion benches use the bench profile (release with debug info); examples and the store bench run with --release.

Synthetic data where a result must be reproducible and machine-independent: deterministic generators with fixed seeds model dependency trees, WinSxS-style hardlink farms, media libraries and hex-named caches.
Index data averages 11.4% directories and about 16.5 name bytes per entry; layout trees use fan-out 16, 20% directories, depth 12 and log-uniform sizes from 1 B to 4 GiB with 2% empty files.
Real data where the operating system is the cost: the standard scanner is timed on a real system volume (about 4.6 million entries) and a generated 1-million-file tree.
MFT parsing is measured on in-memory NTFS images built byte-exactly by the test-image builder, isolating CPU cost from disk speed. Full-drive scans are timed separately with the command-line scanner.

UI frame times come from a headless Chromium (the WebView2 engine) on the real GPU through ANGLE/D3D11. Headless Chromium paces animation frames at 100 Hz, so 100 fps is the ceiling of that measurement.

pnpm --dir ui fixtures:large

groups.title: Open a drive
groups.lede: With admin rights, Strata reads the drive’s Master File Table directly. Without them, a parallel folder scanner fills the same index.

outcomes.label: to parse a million file records from the Master File Table
outcomes.detail: All cores, 3.4–6.4 million records per second. This is parsing speed: reading the table off the drive adds disk time.
outcomes.source: docs/BENCHMARKS.md › Results › MFT scanner › Parse 1M MFT records, parallel: 155–291 ms (3.4–6.4 M records/s)

groups.title: Stay current
groups.lede: Strata follows the NTFS change journal, so open views update in place instead of rescanning.

outcomes.label: to absorb 500,000 files created at once

comparison.machine: 8-core / 16-thread desktop, 32 GB RAM, NVMe SSD, Windows 11
methodology: Same machine, same volume, elevated session for every tool, run back to back with Strata first. No cache was dropped and there was no reboot beforehand.
Wall-clock time from start until the tool has a complete size total for the drive.
Strata: strata-cli MFT scan, which reads the Master File Table unbuffered, so the OS file cache does not help it. WizTree: command-line scan with a minimal CSV export.

Windows File Explorer: the Properties dialog on everything Select all picks in the drive root, which is how you see what fills a drive in Explorer. Timed from opening the dialog until its Size, Size on disk and Contains fields stop changing, read with UI Automation. Explorer leaves out hidden and protected items, so it totals less of the drive than the other tools.
Peak memory is the peak working set of the measured process. Explorer has no process of its own for this, so it is not reported.
Each tool at the version listed, default settings.
